answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. This holds because a newly minted alias starts worthless, so the attacker must first farm credibility on each one before it can swing a verdict. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation. Consider a pulse as the anchor of the cost.
